document: The half race registry of this release: every half-marathon race key with rows, of either source database, as a race with the label a visitor reads, its name and place and the release keys it holds. analysis/half_race_registry.py rebuilds `races` from the release’s tier table and `reviewed`, and stops on any difference; analysis/half_races.py and the runner lookup read races from this file.

rule.key: a release key of a half edition is its source database ("half": the half database; "full": the half editions the marathon database holds) and its key; every key with rows is in exactly one race
rule.join: a key joins a race only by a reviewed join of this file; a key with no entry is its own race; no key joins by similarity; keys that would give a race two editions of one year in one database never join
rule.name: from the key alone: a plain key (no ": ") is its own name and states no separate place; a composite key’s place is the part before the first ": " (without parts that are empty, "TBD" or "?", absent when it is a timing platform’s name) and its name the part after it, HTML entities decoded, a trailing year removed, each word capitalised when the title is all capitals; a reviewed join names its race with a phrase one of its keys states
rule.label: what a visitor reads in a list of races, unique among half races: a plain key’s race takes the key; a reviewed label is taken as written; every other race takes its name, and where two labels would read the same (accents, case and punctuation aside) each such race adds its place in brackets, then its first year, then "marathon database" for a key of the marathon database, then a number in key order; a plain key’s label and a reviewed label never change, so two plain keys that differ only by punctuation keep their keys as their labels

flags.platform_prefix: the part before ": " is a timing platform’s name, so the key states no place
flags.no_half_word_in_title: a composite key whose event title has no half-marathon word (half, halb, halv, semi, demi, medio, media, mezza, meia, mitja, mitad, 21)

rule.order: races are sorted by label (accents and case aside), then by label as written; a race’s keys by first year, then database, then key
